Chunk Text:
The Plant shall be designed as a Combined Cycle Power Plant, consisting of but not limited to:
- Dual Fuel Gas Turbine (GTs)
- Dry low NOx combustors;
- Heat Recovery Steam Generators (HRSGs),
- By-pass  stack  including  diverter  dampers  horizontal  and  vertical  sealing  guillotine damper.
- Condensing Steam Turbine (CST) with Air Cooled Condenser
- Synchronous Generators for Gas Turbines and Steam Turbine
- Generator Circuit Breakers for GTGs and STGs
- 2 winding Generator Step-up transformers;
- 2 or 3 winding Auxiliary transformers
- HV Circuit Breakers for GSU Transformers of GTGs and STG
The plant shall be designed preferably symmetrically; this means the Plant shall consist of equally designed Groups (same number and type of GTs/HRSGs/ST).

Chunk Text:
The steam turbine outlet connection pieces shall be designed for smooth transition with minimal obstructions from the LP turbine exhaust to the condenser to assure negligible pressure drop.
The turbine bypass dumps shall be designed with dispersion headers internal to the condenser to adequately disperse the steam safely into the condenser for all possible extreme transient scenarios.
The Air-Cooled condenser materials shall be selected to provide the necessary reliability at an economical cost taking into account that ACC is being operated with Demineralized water with proper water chemistry required by OEM guidelines. ACC OEM Design will take into consideration of proper material selection as per Demin water quality..
Vacuum raising and maintaining plant may be based on either steam ejectors or mechanical vacuum pumps. As a minimum, one start-up (hogging) duty and one running duty device shall be provided for each condenser.
Steam for air ejectors, if supplied, shall be taken from the main steam supply. A silencer shall be provided on each ejector outlet.
The hotwell tank and condensate system shall be sized in accordance with HEI standards.
The condensate system shall be equipped with instrumentation that will assist in trouble shooting of any condenser tube leakage.

All  pumps  and  compressors  shall  be  redundant  with  on-line  switchover  capability  with  following redundancy:
- Pumps, blowers, compressors, fans : N+1
- Lube oil pump for HP Feedwater Pump : 2x100% (for each FW pump)
- Lube oil heater for HP Feedwater Pump : 2x100% (for each FW pump)
- Power Plant Jockey pumps : 2x100%
- Heat exchangers (not applicable to fin fan cooler or to air cooled condenser). Redundancy should be considered to eliminate single point of failure that will result in reduced load.
- Cooling tower/fin fan cooler cells : N+1
- Tanks (if not mentioned hereunder) : more than 1
- CCW Expansion Tanks : 1 x 100%
- Atmospheric drain tank : 1 x 100%
- Vacuum Flash Tank : 1 x 100%
- Condensate Storage Tank : 2x50% or 1x100%
- Service air receiver tank : 2 x 100%
- Instrument air receiver tank : 2 x 100%
- H2 Tanks : 2 x 50%
- Diesel storage tank : 2 x 50%
- Gas Drain Collection Tank (GT Area) : 1 x 100%
- GT Fuel Gas Last Chance Filter (per GT) : 2 x 100% Chemical tanks
- DM plant : N+1 stream
- Air conditioning :  N+1  (except  for  non-plant  buildings,  such  as: Administration building/ workshop/warehouse/Gate guard house)
- Ventilation Fans :  N+1  (except  for  non-plant  buildings,  such  as: Administration building/ workshop/warehouse/Gate guard house))
- Gas reducing station : 3 x 50%
- Feed water control stations : 2 x 100%
- Fuel Gas Boosting Compressors: : N+1, where, N=Number of Gas Turbines
- Air  compressors  with  after  coolers  (after  coolers  if  required,  will  be  confirmed  during  detail engineering) : 3x50%
- Air filtering skids : 2 x 100%
- Air dryers : 2 x 100%
- After Filters : 2 x 100%
- CO2 rack & manifold station for each GT : 1 x 100%
- CO2 rack & manifold station for each ST : 1 x 100%
- N2 rack & manifold station : 1 x 100%
- H2 generator : 2 x 100%
- Drain and vent valves :  two  valves  in  series  (If  operating  pressure  is greater than 4 MPa) otherwise single valve
- Level control valve for HRSG Drums and Feedwater tank :  N+1 (not applicable for startup line, as applicable)
Provision of bypass valves for control valves shall apply for those systems/facilities which can also be reasonably controlled manually.

Performance correction curves and formulae for the correction of measured performance data at conditions different from the Reference Conditions shall be provided by the contractor for both the primary and the backup fuel:
- Gas Turbine Standard correction curves
- Gas Turbine generator capability curve
- Steam Turbine generator capability curve
- CC Start-up curves
- CC Shutdown curve
- Capacity of GT system vs ambient temperature
- Gas Turbine GSUT capacity curve
- Response capability curve (frequency response chart)
- Emissions table
- Steam turbine load changes
- Power output vs gas pressure
- CC Correction curves (to be provided for):
- Evaporative Cooler ON (Only for Base Load),
- Wet Compression On (only after Evaporative Cooler is ON)
- Evaporative Cooler OFF (Base Load and partial loads)
- Duct Firing On (if applicable)
- o The corrections of the net capacity and net heat rate of the total Plant in combined cycle configuration shall be provided for:
- ambient air temperature
- ambient air humidity
- ambient barometric pressure
- Fuel Gas Lower Heating value (LHV)
- Fuel Gas C:H ratio
- Inlet  Air  Condition  Difference  Between  Cooling  Tower/ACC  and  Gas Turbine
- Grid Frequency
- Power Factor
- Cycle Unaccounted Losses
- Natural Gas Pressure at the Terminal Point
- Natural Gas Temperature at the Terminal Point
- Partial load (only for EVC OFF case)
- Degradation with GT fired hours
- condensate return flow and temperature
- b. Outage modes
The important and different outage modes encountered during the operation shall be furnished by the Contractor. Corresponding H&M balance drawings are to be supplied by the Contractor.
The outage durations of GT, HRSG and ST shall be defined.
The  outage  frequency  shall  be  defined  for  HRSG,  ST  and  GT  (in  line  with  the  typical  LTSA assumptions).

- Turbine drain system, complete,

- Fire protection equipment,
- All connecting piping, bearings, fittings, safety devices, fastenings, etc.,

Air cooled condenser(s) will be required to let down steam from the condensing part of the steam turbine and from the LP-steam headers.
The system shall comprise at least the following equipment:
- steam duct from the steam reducing stations to condenser and steam distribution ducting,
- steam duct from turbine exhaust flange to condenser and steam distribution ducting,
- condensate collection headers,
- air moving system,
- fan drives,
- steel support structure, including maintenance platforms, access stairways and escape ladder,
- facilities for prevention of air recirculation,
- noise attenuation features/devices as required,
- all  required  electrical  and  control  equipment  for  safe  operation,  monitoring  and  measuring, earthing and lightning protection,
- air evacuation pumps, if applicable,
- ejector condenser, drain tank and strainers at ejector steam inlets,
- condensate tank and drain,
- drain and vent pumping, piping, valves and traps with supports, and
- semi-automatic ACC outside heat transfer surface cleaning system.
The steam turbine condenser shall be complete in every respect for reliable, efficient and safe operation for a high service lifetime. The design of the air-cooled condenser shall be in accordance with the ambient conditions at Project Site and steam turbine requirements.
The condenser shall be sized to receive:
- Condense all steam for all operating ranges
- Accept the full steam turbine bypass steam when the steam turbine trips.
The  capacity  of  the  steam  turbine  condenser  shall  include  a  reserve  to  cover  possible  steam  turbine overloads.

Chunk Text:
The cooling air to each heat exchanging cell shall be forced by individual axial flow fan; each fan, whose blades shall be adjustable when the fan is out of service, shall be driven by a variable speed motor.
All the components of the fan/drive unit shall be designed for continuous outdoor service over the range of air condenser loads, ambient air temperatures and air temperatures adjacent to the tube bundles.
It shall be possible to initiate a cold start of the fans during any ambient air temperature within the specified range.
All drive components shall be rated to take into account any shock loading that may occur from starting a fan which may be rotating in a reverse direction under the influence of prevailing winds or convection currents. As an alternative, a reverse rotation lock may be provided.
Each fan drive shall be individually remotely controlled from the Control Room allowing the operator to optimize the operative configuration on the basis of actual ambient condition.

The shaft vibration (not bearing vibration) high alarm and trip functions will be provided.
Over speed Trip interlock test will be carried out after Gas turbine reaches full speed no load.
